tasks.title: P27-01 — Planner identity de-duplication, the empty-span guard and one window rule (D77, D82, D83)
tasks.description: In services/backfill_service.py make plan_requests emit one plan per request identity (endDateTime, duration, bar_size) and none for a span with no positive length, and make _bar_level_missing_spans use half-open [start, end) window membership (a window capped by now keeps t <= now_ts) with one gap_threshold = period * 1.5 for the leading, internal and trailing edges. present_days is NOT changed — its equity membership stays window_start <= ts <= window_end and its futures branch and signature stay byte-identical; only its docstring gains the statement of that predicate and why it is inclusive at the close. New pure suite tests/test_d77_d82_d83_planner_identity.py; the existing planner/day-presence/history suites must stay green unchanged, including both 1 day params of tests/test_history_backfill.py::test_t40_t04_chunked_multi_request_continuity — a red assertion in the D16/D42 suites is a stop-and-escalate, never a re-baseline.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given any set of spans produced by find_missing_spans, When plan_requests runs, Then no two plans share (endDateTime, duration, bar_size), and the plans' coverage is unchanged by the change and contains every input span (chunk-granularity over-fetch is stated in D77 and idempotent through the cache primary key).
Given the same input, Then every interval that was covered before the change is still covered — a fixture where the floor span starts earlier than the presence span still fetches the earlier part.
Given a coinciding-span scenario, Then exactly one request is spent where the pre-change planner spent two, and the per-load cap is charged once.
Given a bar timestamped exactly at a session's end, When the planner runs, Then the bar is counted in exactly one window (never two) and no span is emitted for the boundary instant.

Given a trailing hole of 1.0 period and of 1.7/2.0 periods, When the planner runs, Then the 1.0-period hole is not reported and the 1.7- and 2.0-period holes are; the module docstring and the code state the same number (1.5 bar periods).
Given a span whose end equals its start, When plan_requests runs, Then it emits no plan for it, and a list containing only such spans yields an empty plan list.

Given a ten-trading-day '1 day' cache whose bars are stamped at the session close (16:00 ET), When present_days runs under either mode and find_missing_spans runs with now at the last close, Then all ten days are present and no span is produced, a test-local half-open variant of the same predicate returns 0 of 10 on the same series, an intraday out-of-mode day is still absent, and present_days' signature, equity membership expression and futures branch are unchanged.

tests.description: Build Journey 71's out-of-mode fixture (ETH-cached bars, RTH load with min_sessions=30) and a hand-built two-span list whose spans share end_ts; run plan_requests on both and compare the identity multiset and the plan count with the pre-change rule's count.
tests.expected_result: No repeated (endDateTime, duration, bar_size) identity in either fixture; the shared anchor yields exactly one plan; the coinciding-span fixture's plan count is exactly the pre-change count minus the number of duplicated identities.

tests.description: Partially overlapping pair where the floor span starts earlier than the presence span. The test derives the expected anchor set from the input spans with its own chunk arithmetic (the pre-change rule, independent of the implementation), then asserts each expected anchor is planned exactly once, the floor span's earlier part is still covered, and every input span is contained in the union of planned intervals.
tests.expected_result: Every independently derived anchor is present exactly once; the earlier part of the floor span is still fetched; coverage before the change is reproduced and every input span is contained in the plans' coverage.

tests.description: Two spans sharing the same end instant but carrying different configured durations/bar sizes (two different timeframes' plans side by side) are passed to plan_requests.
tests.expected_result: Two plans are emitted — the identity key is all three fields (endDateTime, duration, bar_size), so an anchor/duration difference is not de-duplicated away.

tests.description: plan_requests([MissingSpan(t, t)], tf) and plan_requests([MissingSpan(t, t), MissingSpan(u, u)], tf) with a non-negative-span control case.
tests.expected_result: A zero-length span emits no plan, a list of only zero-length spans yields [], and the control case still plans its request.

tests.description: A complete 5 mins RTH session (bars through 15:55 ET), plus a bar stamped exactly at the session end (16:00 ET) and the next session's first bar, run through the bar-level gap pass under RTH.
tests.expected_result: The closing window accounts the 15:55 bar last (the 16:00 bar is not counted in it), no span is emitted for the boundary instant, and every counted instant appears in exactly one window's accounting.

tests.description: Three trailing-hole fixtures above the planner's last accounted bar: 1.0 period, 1.7 periods and 2.0 periods; read the threshold number the module docstring states and compare it with the value the fixtures bracket.
tests.expected_result: The 1.0-period hole yields no span; the 1.7-period and 2.0-period holes each yield one span; the docstring states 1.5 bar periods, the same number the two fixtures bracket.

tests.description: A ten-trading-day '1 day' cache whose bars are stamped 16:00 ET (the tree's own daily fixture convention), read by present_days under ext_hours False and True and by find_missing_spans with now at the last close; plus a test-local half-open variant of the same predicate computed inside the test (not imported from the module), an intraday pre/post-only day under RTH, and an intraday series whose only bar sits exactly at the mode's window end.
tests.expected_result: present_days returns all ten days under both modes; find_missing_spans returns []; the test-local half-open variant returns 0 of 10 on the same series; the intraday out-of-mode day is absent; the intraday close-instant bar's day is present.

tests.description: Journey 71's edges through find_missing_spans plus plan_requests: a partial floor (cache covering only part of the floor window), an empty cache with the floor enabled, and a cache holding exactly one in-mode bar.
tests.expected_result: The partial floor still plans its earlier part; the empty cache with the floor enabled produces one plan (not two coerced from coinciding spans); the single-in-mode-bar cache produces no bar-level span.

tasks.title: P27-02 — D78: the prime's backstop is armed for the retry's own deadline
tasks.description: In ui/ticker_session.py add module constants _PRIME_BACKSTOP_MS = 15_000 and _PRIME_RETRY_GRACE_MS = 1_000 and the helper _prime_backstop_ms(retry_ms) returning max(_PRIME_BACKSTOP_MS, retry_ms + _PRIME_RETRY_GRACE_MS). In prime_aggregator's PacingExceeded branch compute retry_ms = max(1000, int(wait_s * 1000)) once, pass that same value to the one QTimer.singleShot (call shape unchanged) and start _prime_timer at _prime_backstop_ms(retry_ms); the issued-prime branch keeps the flat 15_000, and the surrounding comment states that the backstop covers the retry's deferral and the answer to an issued prime. _on_prime_timeout, _on_prime_retry, _fail_open_prime and prepare_load are not changed, no timer or settings key is added, and no pacing constant is retuned — the quantified worst case is AC-D78.3's 'reported wait plus the backstop' branch, not a new stall.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a pacing refusal with wait > 15 s and a fake clock, When the clock reaches the reported wait, Then the prime issues a request — the deferral backstop never pre-empts the retry, so at 15 s and at wait-minus-epsilon the retry is still pending and nothing was attached.

Given a prime that is issued and never answers, When the backstop elapses, Then the live feed attaches exactly once and no second request follows; a retry that is itself refused fails open once with no further attempt.

Given any pacing refusal, Then the time from refusal to an issued prime or a fail-open attach is bounded by the reported wait plus the backstop and is never unbounded, including the historical-wait ceiling (wait=600 → deferral backstop 601_000 ms, refusal-to-attach at most 616 s).

Given a wait at or below 14 s, Then the deferral backstop is exactly 15_000 ms (today's value preserved), a wait of exactly 15 s arms 16_000 ms so the retry fires first, and no pacing constant is retuned and no settings key is added.

tests.description: Fake clock/host with a stub md_manager counting req_historical_data calls and a historical_wait_seconds stub returning 40 s; run prime_aggregator, then advance the clock to 15 s, to wait-minus-epsilon and to the wait.
tests.expected_result: _prime_retry_pending is True and _prime_timer.interval() == 41_000 after the refusal; at 15 s and at wait-minus-epsilon nothing was attached and the retry is still pending; at 40 s the retry runs and _prime_req_id is set.

tests.description: The same fixture with wait=2 s.
tests.expected_result: _prime_timer.interval() is exactly 15_000 (today's value) and the retry fires at 2 s, issuing a priming request.

tests.description: The same fixture with wait exactly 15 s (the boundary the grace tick exists for).
tests.expected_result: _prime_timer.interval() is 16_000 and the retry fires before the backstop; nothing was attached at the 15 s instant.

tests.description: An issued prime whose request never answers: let the backstop elapse with a host attach spy and a request counter.
tests.expected_result: The attach spy is called exactly once and exactly one priming request was ever issued — no second attempt.

tests.description: For several waits including the historical-wait ceiling (wait=600 s), measure refusal→(issued prime or attach) on the fake clock and read the armed interval.
tests.expected_result: At wait=600 the armed interval is 601_000 ms and refusal-to-attach never exceeds wait + 1 s + 15 s (616 s), while the issued-prime bound stays 15 s.

tests.description: Journey 72's edges: a retry that is itself refused, a new load issued during the deferral, and a disconnect during the deferral.
tests.expected_result: The refused retry fails open exactly once with no third attempt; the new load's own prime governs and the stale singleShot callback is a no-op; the disconnect leaves the pending callback harmless (no attach from it).

expected_artifacts: ui/ticker_session.py — _PRIME_BACKSTOP_MS, _PRIME_RETRY_GRACE_MS, _prime_backstop_ms(retry_ms), and prime_aggregator's deferral branch (retry_ms computed once, backstop armed from it) plus its restated comment

the frozen prime signatures in docs/architecture.md § Phase P27 § Frozen Interfaces
outputs: a deferral backstop derived from the retry's own deadline
the flat 15 s answer bound preserved for an issued prime

tasks.title: P27-03a — D81: budget is stamped only by a send that crossed the wire
tasks.description: Split the pacing gate from the stamp: ibkr/pacing.py gets def throttle(self, *, stamp: bool = True) -> bool whose reservation branch is byte-identical (decrement, return True), else reads request_wait_seconds() (raising PacingExceeded when closed), stamps only when stamp is true, and returns False. In ibkr/market_data.py the four generic paths become readiness → reserved = pacing_manager.throttle(stamp=False) → req_id = id_manager.get_id() → try: self.client.req…(…) / except Exception: id_manager.release_id(req_id); raise → if not reserved: pacing_manager.record_request_slot() → return req_id; req_historical_data moves its existing historical_wait_seconds() gate in front of get_id() and keeps its after-send stamp. Add IdManager.release_id(req_id) -> bool (under the lock, roll back only when self._next_id - 1 == req_id) and give the two pacing doubles the keyword-only parameter; the default path stays behaviour-identical, pinned by tests/test_d28_pacing.py::test_throttle_success_stamps_interval_gate and P26's replay suite, both unchanged. New suite cases (a),(b),(c),(f) only — cases (d) and (e) belong to P27-T4.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a client whose request call raises, When the request is attempted, Then the pacing interval clock and the realtime/historical budgets are unchanged by the attempt, and the next successful request is spaced from the previous successful one.

Given the same failing send, Then the id sequence has no gap caused by a failed send — after the failing send the next successful request receives the id the failed attempt took, and release_id rolls back only the newest allocation.

Given a generic_batch(3) reservation, When three req_mkt_data sends run inside it, Then three reservation units are consumed, the sends do not stamp _last_req_time, and the batch's exit stamps once; an empty generic_batch(0) reserves nothing, leaves the gate deciding and stamps nothing.

Given a caller that does not pass stamp=False, When throttle runs, Then it behaves exactly as today — raising PacingExceeded carrying the reported wait when the gate is closed, stamping on success, consuming one reservation unit inside a batch — and returns whether a reservation unit was spent.

tests.description: A fake client whose chosen call raises, a monkeypatched clock, and a pacing manager reset between cases: perform a successful send, then a raising send, then a successful send on the same path.
tests.expected_result: The interval between the first and third successful sends is exactly one minimum interval (the failed attempt consumed none), and the historical and realtime budget counters are identical before and after the failed attempt.

tests.description: The same failing-send fixture, observing the ids handed to the client and to the caller.
tests.expected_result: The next successful request receives the same id the failed attempt took — the id sequence has no failure-shaped gap.

tests.description: Call release_id on a real IdManager wrapper: once with the newest allocation, once with a non-newest id, and once after another get_id.
tests.expected_result: The newest allocation rolls back and returns True (the next get_id returns that id again); a non-newest id returns False and changes nothing.

tests.description: Inside pacing_manager.generic_batch(3), issue three req_mkt_data sends; separately, inside generic_batch(0), issue one send with the gate open and one with it closed.
tests.expected_result: Three sends consume three reservation units and leave _last_req_time untouched inside the batch, with one stamp at the batch's exit; the empty batch reserves nothing and stamps nothing, so the gate decides each send.

tests.description: Call throttle() with no argument in three states — gate closed, gate open, and inside an open generic_batch reservation.
tests.expected_result: Closed: raises PacingExceeded carrying the reported wait and stamps nothing; open: stamps once and returns False; inside a reservation: consumes one unit, leaves the clock untouched and returns True.

expected_artifacts: ibkr/pacing.py — throttle(*, stamp: bool = True) -> bool with its docstring stating the two modes
ibkr/market_data.py — the four generic request bodies reordered (readiness → gate → id → send-try → stamp) and req_historical_data's gate moved before get_id

tasks.title: P27-RW1 — the D81 signature change's test-double sweep: keyword-stamped `throttle` doubles + the guard
tasks.description: P27-RW1 — the D81 signature change's test-double sweep. P27-T3 made `PacingManager.throttle` keyword-only `stamp` (default True) and `ibkr/market_data.py` calls `throttle(stamp=False)` at three request sites (`:111`, `:142`, `:177`), so every `throttle` double installed in `tests/` must accept the keyword form. The guard is a **static AST scan with zero exemptions**: a `lambda: None` is rejected whether or not its path can reach the real call, so "behaviourally unreachable" is not "out of scope" here. All eight zero-argument doubles in the tree therefore change from `lambda: None` to `lambda *, stamp=True: None` — the three the signature change breaks today (`tests/test_d65_option_stream.py:191`, `tests/test_d27_reconnect.py:148`, `tests/test_d45_removal.py:516`) and the five whose paths stub the generic request seam (`win.md_manager.req_historical_data`, `win.rt_manager.subscribe`) or drive RT-bar/historical paths, so no `req_mkt_data` / `req_contract_details` / `req_sec_def_opt_params` call reaches them (`tests/test_d27_aggregator_priming.py:26`, `tests/test_d48_mode_parity.py:118`, `tests/test_d67_forming_candle.py:569`, `tests/test_d27_stream_health.py:56`, `tests/test_d41_removal.py:252`); in those five the edit is signature conformance alone, so every assertion and every other line of every one of the eight files stays untouched. One further in-footprint change is required and permitted: `tests/test_d65_option_stream.py`'s `_make_window` also installs `monkeypatch.setattr(pacing_mod.pacing_manager, "record_request_slot", lambda: None)` — the same class of harness double. D81 moved the interval stamp out of `throttle()` into `record_request_slot()`; without the stub the 16 leg sends stamp the generic interval, `generic_wait_for_batch(16)` returns 0.3 s, and P26's all-or-nothing `replay_all` defers the reconnect replay via a `QTimer.singleShot` that never fires under pytest, yielding 0 new `reqMktData`. The stub is scheduling-only: no production line changes and the asserted `reqMktData` counts are unchanged. Add `tests/test_p27_throttle_double_signature.py`: an AST guard that discovers every `throttle` double in `tests/` at run time (each `monkeypatch.setattr(<expr>, "throttle", <callable>)` and each `def throttle(...)`) and fails unless it accepts `throttle(stamp=False)` with zero exemptions, plus a pin on the real keyword-only signature and a negative control proving a zero-argument double is rejected. The five doubles that passed before the fix are covered by that same guard, not exempted — each now carries the same `lambda *, stamp=True: None` form: `tests/test_d27_aggregator_priming.py:26`, `tests/test_d48_mode_parity.py:118`, `tests/test_d67_forming_candle.py:569`, `tests/test_d27_stream_health.py:56` and `tests/test_d41_removal.py:252` were unreachable only because their paths stub the generic request seam (`win.md_manager.req_historical_data`, `win.rt_manager.subscribe`) or drive RT-bar/historical paths, so no `req_mkt_data` / `req_contract_details` / `req_sec_def_opt_params` call reaches the double — safety here is enforced by the guard, never assumed. Nothing else changes: no production edit, no pacing constant, no other test's assertions (the option-stream `record_request_slot` stub above is the sole harness addition); the guard lives in its own file rather than in `tests/test_p27_fence.py` because P27-T5 owns that file, already holds a written skeleton and will be re-dispatched as a finalize worker — T6 writing it would either serialize against an in-flight task or be lost when the fence is regenerated, and P27-T5 now depends on P27-T6 so the finalize pass runs after this fix and can verify the green suite. Exit condition: the full offscreen suite (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen .venv/bin/python -m pytest -m 'not webengine' -q`) is green except `tests/test_d64_batch_gate.py::test_p22_t5_ac2_shared_seam_record`, which asserts a clean `tests/` tree and can only pass once the phase is committed — record it as exactly that, do not fix it here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given `ibkr/pacing.py`, Then `PacingManager.throttle` declares `stamp` as a KEYWORD-ONLY parameter defaulting to `True` — it is never positional, the default is not changed, and the three `MarketDataManager` request sites still call `throttle(stamp=False)`.

Given every `throttle` double installed anywhere under `tests/` — each `monkeypatch.setattr(<expr>, "throttle", <callable>)` and each `def throttle(...)` in a test helper class — Then every one of them accepts `throttle(stamp=False)` and `throttle()` (its `stamp` is keyword-only with a default, or it declares `**kwargs`); the set is discovered from the tree at run time with zero exemptions, so a double added by a later phase is covered without editing the guard, and a zero-argument double is rejected by the guard's own negative control.

Given the phase tree, Then the three pre-existing tests the signature change broke pass — `tests/test_d65_option_stream.py::test_P23_T9_AC1_on_populates_both_ladders_negative_and_partial_legs`, `tests/test_d27_reconnect.py::test_d27_3_drop_reconnect_reissues_with_rebound_reqids` and `tests/test_d45_removal.py::test_zero_transmit_walkthrough` — with their assertions unchanged; in each file the only edits are the installed `throttle` double's signature and, in `tests/test_d65_option_stream.py`'s `_make_window` only, a `monkeypatch.setattr(pacing_mod.pacing_manager, "record_request_slot", lambda: None)` pacing-seam stub (the same class of harness double): D81 moved the interval stamp from `throttle()` into `record_request_slot()`, so without it the 16 leg sends consume the generic interval and P26's all-or-nothing `replay_all` defers the reconnect replay via a `QTimer.singleShot` that never fires under pytest; the stub is scheduling-only — it skips pacing bookkeeping in the harness, touches no production line, and leaves every asserted `reqMktData` count unchanged.

Given the full offscreen suite run as `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen .venv/bin/python -m pytest -m 'not webengine' -q`, Then it reports no failure attributable to a `throttle` double or to this phase's code, and the one exception is recorded explicitly: `tests/test_d64_batch_gate.py::test_p22_t5_ac2_shared_seam_record` asserts a clean `tests/` working tree and can only pass once the phase is committed, so it is a post-commit gate, not a code defect and not fixed here.

contracts.signature: `ThrottleDouble(path: str, lineno: int, kind: Literal["setattr", "def"], accepts_keyword_stamp: bool)`; `discover_throttle_doubles(tests_dir: Path) -> list[ThrottleDouble]` walks every `tests/**/*.py` via `ast`, collecting (a) `Call` nodes whose func is `setattr` with a literal `"throttle"` second argument and (b) `FunctionDef` named `throttle`; `accepts_keyword_stamp(expr, module_ast) -> bool` is True iff the callable is an `ast.Lambda` or `FunctionDef` with `stamp` in `kwonlyargs` (and a default) or a non-None `kwarg` (**kwargs), or an `ast.Name`/`ast.Attribute` resolving to such a module-level definition — anything unresolvable FAILS naming `path:lineno`; tests: `test_real_throttle_signature_is_keyword_only_stamp()`, `test_every_throttle_double_accepts_keyword_stamp[<path:lineno>]` (parametrized over the discovery, asserting the eight fixed files and both class doubles are in the discovered set), `test_guard_rejects_zero_argument_doubles()` (negative control over in-test synthetic source). The installed double's fixed form is exactly `lambda *, stamp=True: None`.
